videos.hook:
Your Mac,
but it wakes up
in a museum.
videos.caption: A quiet little museum that lives in your Mac menu bar. With Museum Mat enabled (the default), each painting is composed instead of cropped.

videos.hook:
Portrait monitor owners:
I fixed the wallpaper problem.
videos.proof: EaselWall matches paintings to each display's orientation.
videos.caption: Portrait art for portrait displays. Landscape art for landscape displays. It should have worked this way all along.

videos.proof: Choose a unique painting for every connected display.
videos.caption: One Mac setup, three different paintings—each fitted to its own display.

videos.hook:
No account.
No feed.
No notifications.
Just art.
videos.proof: No ads, subscriptions, or tracking in the app.
videos.caption: An app you install once and then mostly forget—until tomorrow's painting appears.

videos.hook:
53 works.
No repeats within
each orientation cycle.
videos.proof: Thirty paintings are included for offline use.
videos.caption: Van Gogh, Monet, Cassatt, Degas, Renoir, Cezanne and Seurat—curated for a calmer desktop.

videos.hook:
What if your Mac
had a Monet week?
videos.proof: Tomorrow chooses another work from the collection.
videos.caption: Water lilies today. Pourville tomorrow. A tiny changing exhibition for your desktop.

videos.hook:
Van Gogh,
without The Starry Night.
videos.proof: A quieter way to rediscover familiar artists.
videos.caption: The Bedroom, Weeping Tree, Fishing in Spring and a self-portrait—there is more to Van Gogh than one night sky.

videos.hook:
A tiny museum
in your menu bar.
videos.caption: EaselWall turns a different public-domain masterpiece into a properly composed Mac wallpaper every day.
